newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate up, baht lower late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate up, baht lower late.

text.p: The Thai interbank overnight rate edged up further from its morning level to 10.00-10.25 percent as lenders were reluctant to offer at lower rates ahead of a public holiday on Tuesday, dealers said.
"There were not many deals. Banks were reluctant to lend and borrowers need funds only at the start of new reserve requirement later this month," one dealer said.
All commercial banks have to meet the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
The interbank overnight rate was quoted around 9.75-10.00 percent this morning and 9.00-9.50 percent late Friday.
The baht eased further against the dollar to 25.566-25.569 from 25.557-25.560 early in line with the upward trend of the dollar/yen rate.
"There has been some dollar buying ahead of holiday in anticipation that the dollar might continue to rise," said a dealer from one local bank.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium fell to 8.00/9.00 satangs per dollar versus 9.00/9.50 satangs in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.53 against 25.52 on Friday.
